## Appearance

Uncle Jim is a homely man with a tall, ungainly, and somewhat stooped figure that nevertheless suggests great strength and endurance. His clean-shaven face is deeply lined and bronzed, featuring spare jaws, a rugged mouth, a square brow, and clear, remarkably deep-set blue eyes that sometimes twinkle or dream. He has a thick mane of iron-gray hair falling to his shoulders, though as he grew older, his hair turned much grayer, his hand shook slightly, and he appeared frail and bent.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P15](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0015), [v4 CHAPTER 30 LESLIE DECIDES P3](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0003), [v4 CHAPTER 30 LESLIE DECIDES P11](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0011)_

## Personality

Captain Jim is a rare, high-souled, and simple-minded old man possessing an unfailing, placid cheerfulness that makes it nearly impossible to anger him. A passionate worshipper of beauty, he derives a deep inner joy from every lovely thing he sees or hears. He holds a knack for storytelling and playing the fiddle, though he harbors a deep horror at the thought of a lingering death.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P14](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0014), [v4 CHAPTER 8 MISS CORNELIA BRYANT COMES TO CALL P61](../source/v04-c08.md#nw-v04-c08-p0061), [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P5](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 16 NEW YEAR’S EVE AT THE LIGHT P6](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0006), [v4 CHAPTER 16 NEW YEAR’S EVE AT THE LIGHT P9](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0009), [v4 CHAPTER 17 A FOUR WINDS WINTER P18](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0018), +2 more_

## History

As a young man who hailed from a line of sea-going relatives on his mother's side, Uncle Jim ran off to sea and spent years sailing around the world, collecting material and curiosities from his travels. He welcomed [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Gilbert Blythe](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) upon their arrival in [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds), quickly bonding with them and introducing [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) to the lighthouse. Uncle Jim shared his personal life-book with [Owen Ford](../character/owen-ford.md), who turned the captain's extraordinary life stories and the tragedy of his lost sweetheart into a published novel. He offered spiritual comfort to [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) during her grief, provided a mortgage to assist with a medical procedure for [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md), and was honored when [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) and [Gilbert](../character/gilbert-blythe.md) named their newborn son James Matthew after him. Before his death, Uncle Jim entrusted his cat [First Mate](../character/first-mate.md) to Anne's care, gave his blessing to [Leslie](../character/leslie-moore.md) and Owen's romance, and bequeathed his museum of curiosities to young [Jem](../character/jem.md). He passed away peacefully on his sofa after receiving and reading the completed print copy of his life story.

_Sources: [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P0](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0000), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P7](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0007), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P16](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0016), [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P31](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0031), [v4 CHAPTER 7 THE SCHOOLMASTER’S BRIDE P5](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0005), [v4 CHAPTER 7 THE SCHOOLMASTER’S BRIDE P48](../source/v04-c07.md#nw-v04-c07-p0048), +59 more_

## Quotes

> "Nephew Alec. He understands it as well as I do. Well, now, I’m real glad you asked me to stay to supper. I’m proper hungry—didn’t have much of a dinner today."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P19](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0019)

> “Oh, I do, Mistress Doctor, I do,” protested Captain Jim. “Why, I live like a king gen’rally. Last night I was up to the Glen and took home two pounds of steak. I meant to have a spanking good dinner today.”
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 6 CAPTAIN JIM P21](../source/v04-c06.md#nw-v04-c06-p0021)

> "The Government don’t give lighthouse keepers such luxuries. Look at the colors that wood makes. If you’d like some driftwood for your fire, Mistress Blythe, I’ll bring you up a load some day. Sit down. I’m going to make you a cup of tea."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P24](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0024)

> "That’s Marshall Elliott—a mighty fine man with jest one streak of foolishness in him. I s’pose you wondered what his object was in turning himself into a sort of dime museum freak."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 9 AN EVENING AT FOUR WINDS POINT P32](../source/v04-c09.md#nw-v04-c09-p0032)

> "Yes, I called in on my way home to see him. He’s getting round all right—but stewing in a broth of trouble, as usual, poor man."
>
> — Uncle Jim — [v4 CHAPTER 18 SPRING DAYS P29](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0029)

### [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) · [the relationship](../relationships/anne-shirley--uncle-jim.md)

Captain Jim and [Anne Shirley](../character/anne-shirley.md) are close friends and kindred spirits who enjoy spending time together. They bonded quickly after she moved to [Four Winds](../codex/places.md#four-winds), where Captain Jim welcomed her into his home, shared tea, and entertained her with local lore and tales from his seafaring past. [Anne](../character/anne-shirley.md) frequents his lighthouse to hear his stories, and Captain Jim visits her home to share memories and bring gifts for her garden.
